description: Reader persona definitions for DataStack documentation. All page specs reference these by code (P1–P4).

P1.name: Evaluator
knows: Research data management concepts at a high level
does_not_know: RDF, triples, ontologies, or the semantic web
P1.goal: Assess whether DataStack fits their lab or institution — understand outputs and find the right entry point.
P1.key_gap: No technical background assumed. Needs concept-first explanations with real-world outcomes before any system detail.

P2.name: Operator
P2.tagline: I need to deploy and run this.
knows: Basic networking: ports, URLs, reverse proxies
Reading and editing YAML and JSON
does_not_know: What a triple store is or why it exists
P2.goal: Get the stack deployed, configured, and running reliably.
P2.key_gap: Strong on infrastructure, zero on semantics. Semantic explanations should be deferred or skipped — ops context only.

P3.name: Data Engineer
P3.tagline: I need to wire this into my data workflow.
knows: Tabular data and data transformation concepts
does_not_know: RDF, triples, or the semantic web stack
YARRRML, RML, or any mapping language
What a named graph or blank node is
P3.goal: Connect data sources, author mappings, and query transformation results.
P3.key_gap: Solid general engineering skills but semantic web is completely foreign. Every RDF/SPARQL/YARRRML concept must be explained from first principles — do not assume any prior semantic knowledge.

P4.name: Domain Scientist
P4.tagline: I have data and I want FAIR outputs.
knows: Their scientific domain deeply (materials science, microscopy, lab procedures)
Measurement concepts and experimental workflows they consider universal
Domain-specific tools (OMERO, ELN systems, instrument software)
does_not_know: Ontology terms like PMDCO, CHAMEO, EMMO even if these describe their own work
How ontologies model domain concepts — that this modeling discipline exists at all
SPARQL, RDF, or any semantic technology
P4.goal: Upload their data, trigger the pipeline, and use or export FAIR-compliant results.
P4.key_gap: Double gap: (1) no semantic web knowledge whatsoever, and (2) domain experts frequently assume their concepts are universal common knowledge when they are not — documentation must not assume shared domain vocabulary and must explain what gets modeled and why, not just how.
